title: In Psalms 108 In What Ways Can We Seek Gods Help In Our Own Struggles And Challenges
paragraphs: Seeking God's Help in Our Struggles: Insights from Psalm 108

Psalm 108 is a stirring combination of praise, dependence, and confident hope in God. It offers believers a profound model for seeking God’s help amid life’s challenges. By studying this Psalm, we can discover practical and spiritual ways to turn to God when we face difficulties, trusting in His power and steadfast love.
1. Begin with Praise and Worship
The Psalm opens with a declaration of steadfastness and a commitment to praise God, even before deliverance comes:
My heart is fixed, O God; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises, even with my glory. -
Psalms 108:1 ASV

In times of difficulty, our natural inclination may be to focus on our problems. Instead, this verse encourages us to anchor our hearts in God’s character and begin with worship. Praising God shifts our perspective from our struggles to His greatness and faithfulness.
2. Seek God Early and Publicly
David declares his intention to praise God among the nations, suggesting both urgency and boldness:
I will give thanks unto thee, O Jehovah, among the peoples; And I will sing praises unto thee among the nations. -
Psalms 108:3 ASV

This shows that we can seek God not only in private but also by publicly acknowledging His sovereignty. Bringing our struggles before God each morning and sharing testimonies of His help can strengthen our faith and encourage others.
3. Trust in God’s Unfailing Love and Faithfulness
David grounds his hope in the steadfast love and faithfulness of God:
For thy lovingkindness is great above the heavens; And thy truth reacheth unto the skies. -
Psalms 108:4 ASV
Remembering God’s past faithfulness enables us to trust Him in current trials. God’s love and truth are unchanging, providing a solid foundation in uncertain times.
4. Pray Boldly for Help
David does not hesitate to ask God for deliverance:
That thy beloved may be delivered, Save with thy right hand, and answer us. -
Psalms 108:6 ASV

We are invited to bring specific requests to God, relying on His power to save. The “right hand” symbolizes God’s strength and ability to rescue. In our struggles, we should pray boldly, knowing God hears and responds to the cries of His beloved.
5. Remember God’s Sovereignty Over Every Situation
The Psalmist acknowledges God’s rule over all nations and circumstances:
God hath spoken in his holiness: I will exult; I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth. -
Psalms 108:7 ASV
Even when we feel powerless, God remains in control. Reflecting on His sovereignty reassures us that nothing happens outside His will and care.
6. Confess Our Limitations and Depend Fully on God
David recognizes that human help is insufficient:
Oh give us help against the adversary; For vain is the help of man. -
Psalms 108:12 ASV
This honest admission reminds us to look beyond our own resources or the resources of others, and to depend fully on God. True deliverance comes from Him alone.
7. Act with Confidence in God’s Promises
The Psalm concludes with a declaration of victory:
Through God we shall do valiantly; For he it is that will tread down our adversaries. -
Psalms 108:13 ASV

Once we have sought God’s help, we can move forward in faith, confident that He will provide strength and victory. Our actions, grounded in trust, reflect a belief that God is both willing and able to deliver.
Conclusion

Psalm 108 teaches us to seek God’s help by beginning with praise, trusting in His steadfast love, boldly presenting our requests, acknowledging His sovereignty, confessing our limitations, and acting in confidence. Through Christ, we have assurance of God’s presence and help in every struggle (Hebrews 4:16 ASV). Let us approach Him with humble hearts and expectant faith.
